I’m on a ChatGPT Work (business) plan and running into a recurring pattern across several features — Skills, the Google Docs/Drive connector, and general context-handling — where ChatGPT either fails outright, falsely reports success, or silently drops everything already established in the conversation.

**Issue 1 — Sudden refusals mid-session**
I’ll be actively creating or updating a skill, or editing a document, and it’s working fine. Then, without any change on my end, it suddenly says it can’t connect / can’t do it anymore. Starting a brand-new chat doesn’t fix it — the same refusal shows up there too.

**Issue 2 — Google Docs connector reports false success**
When asking ChatGPT to edit a live Google Doc via the connector, it sometimes reports the edit as done, but the actual document is unchanged. When I point this out, it acknowledges the edit never went through — so it reported success without the write having actually happened.

**Issue 3 — Stops applying context from earlier in the same conversation**
In the same working session, ChatGPT will suddenly stop connecting to everything already established earlier in that same chat. For example: after reviewing a contract in detail, or setting up exactly how I want something done (a skill), I’ll ask for a follow-up task — like drafting an email — and instead of using what we’d already built, it responds generically, as if it doesn’t know who I am or what we’ve been working on. The emails suddenly sound like they’d write for anyone, with none of the specific context, tone, or instructions already established in that same conversation. Nothing changed on my end — it’s the same chat, same setup, minutes apart.

**Not a usage/rate-limit issue:** I checked Settings → Usage when this happens — I’m nowhere near my caps (100% of my 5-hour limit and 94%+ of my weekly limit remaining). So this isn’t me hitting a quota.

**Pattern:** intermittent, multiple times a week, not tied to conversation length (happens in short new chats too, not just long ones), no visible error code or message beyond a plain refusal, a false “done,” or a sudden loss of context. Work plan.

Has anyone else seen this — is this a known/open issue on OpenAI’s side?

I’m on a ChatGPT Work (business) plan and running into a recurring pattern across several features — Skills, the Google Docs/Drive connector, and general context-handling — where ChatGPT either fails outright, falsely reports success, or silently drops everything already established in the conversation.

**Issue 1 — Sudden refusals mid-session**
I’ll be actively creating or updating a skill, or editing a document, and it’s working fine. Then, without any change on my end, it suddenly says it can’t connect / can’t do it anymore. Starting a brand-new chat doesn’t fix it — the same refusal shows up there too.

**Issue 2 — Google Docs connector reports false success**
When asking ChatGPT to edit a live Google Doc via the connector, it sometimes reports the edit as done, but the actual document is unchanged. When I point this out, it acknowledges the edit never went through — so it reported success without the write having actually happened.

**Issue 3 — Stops applying context from earlier in the same conversation**
In the same working session, ChatGPT will suddenly stop connecting to everything already established earlier in that same chat. For example: after reviewing a contract in detail, or setting up exactly how I want something done (a skill), I’ll ask for a follow-up task — like drafting an email — and instead of using what we’d already built, it responds generically, as if it doesn’t know who I am or what we’ve been working on. The seven features covered here form the baseline specification for any serious industrial installation. A supply that checks all seven will outlast and outperform a general-purpose alternative in virtually any plant application.

external.description:
According to a market analysis published in IEEE Power Electronics Magazine, the global power supply industry generates roughly **$21 billion in annual revenue** , with AC-DC types accounting for $18 billion of that figure. Despite the scale of the market, not all power supplies are built to the same standard – and in industrial settings, the gap between a general-purpose unit and a true industrial-grade design shows up quickly when conditions get rough.

Industrial power supplies**** face demands that consumer or commercial-grade units were never designed for: sustained operation at elevated temperatures, voltage sag from large motor starts, EMC interference from welding or VFDs, and zero tolerance for unplanned shutdowns. The features that distinguish industrial power supplies from the alternatives are measurable engineering decisions with real consequences for system uptime.

This article covers the seven features that consistently separate **industrial-grade power supplies** from the rest.

## **1. What Makes Wide-Range Input Voltage a Non-Negotiable Spec?**

### **How Input Range Affects System Resilience**

record.text: If you use Grok on X, your posts and conversations may be used to train xAI’s models. Here’s how to opt out in a few steps.

external.description:
If you use Grok on X, there’s a good chance your posts, chats, and interactions could be helping train xAI’s AI models. The good news is that you can turn this off in just a few taps.

xAI lets users opt out of having their public posts and Grok conversations used for AI training through X’s privacy settings. You’ll still be able to use Grok normally, but your interactions won’t be used to train or fine-tune future versions of the model.

## How to turn off Grok AI training

### Step 1: Open the X app or visit X on the web

### Step 2: Go to Settings & Privacy

### Step 3: Tap Privacy & Safety

### Step 4: Scroll to Data sharing and personalization

### Step 5: Select Grok & Third-party Collaborators

### Step 6: Turn off the option that says “Allow your public data as well as your interactions, inputs, and results with Grok and xAI to be used for training and fine-tuning.”

### This post is for subscribers only
